records.source_paraphrase: Rath links fifth/tenth/full-moon tithi observances and Sarasvati/Guru devotion to skill acquisition, mastery and wisdom.
records.caveat: Ritual intervention is not a birth-chart-derived forecast; purported efficacy not independently established.

records.source_paraphrase: The author describes rsi-krta as a teacher/seer's blessing supposedly enabling clairvoyance, citing the Mahabharata story of Sanjaya perceiving a distant battle.
records.caveat: A scriptural narrative is not an independently confirmed sensory or prospective prediction case.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath introduces śikṣā with a paraphrase of higher mind, conduct and wisdom trainings attributed to Buddhism.
records.caveat: This is not a quoted Jaimini sutra or birth-derived claim. Do not treat doctrinal vocabulary as evidence of personality prediction.

records.source_paraphrase: The chandas section associates rhythm and poetic meter with allegedly greater mantra efficacy, illustrated with a tuning-fork analogy.
records.caveat: Analogy is not a measured physical or clinical effect; no natal predictor or controlled mantra test is present.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath uses Pingala/chandas language, Meru Prastara triangles and expansions of meters in an explanatory sequence about creation through sound.
records.caveat: Mathematical triangle construction may be checked arithmetically; historical author dates and cosmological implications are not thereby validated.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath associates reasoning with third/sixth houses and Mercury and logic direction with Mars as part of a four-part schema of knowledge.
records.caveat: Not a narrow independent theorem from a printed Jaimini sutra, and no psychometric validation in source.

records.source_paraphrase: The explanatory course distinguishes a physical birth from later Gayatri initiation as a 'second birth' affecting vocation and identity.
records.caveat: Actual initiation date is observable but the exposition gives no independently tested natal chart forecast of it.

records.source_paraphrase: A source table distributes 16 vowels, 25 consonants and nine semivowels/sibilants into three sound classes associated with Sun, five planets and Moon.
records.caveat: Preserve Sanskrit grapheme/phoneme, conjunct and aspirated distinctions; an English spelling is not a lossless phonetic input.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath defines a vowel as a phoneme that allows otherwise incomplete consonant sounds to manifest, using the distinction in syllabic/varga computation.
records.caveat: Comparative Sanskrit phonology method, not evidence names predict actual traits; exact phoneme segmentation must be specified.

records.source_paraphrase: The author associates ya/ra/la/va with air/fire/earth/water and discusses awareness and material elements.
records.caveat: Four-element symbolism is not a measured biomedical taxonomy or natal planetary rule.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath begins the introductory lesson with meanings of ṛṣi/maharṣi and the title Jaimini Kṛta Upadeśa Sūtra, rather than presenting chart-to-life aphorisms.
records.caveat: Course title does not license attributing every explanatory claim in it to the actual Jaimini sutras.

records.source_paraphrase: Rath explicitly says a single sage can belong to multiple classifications (brahmarṣi, mahārṣi, devarṣi), then connects those religious categories with cosmological levels and planets.
records.caveat: Not independent occupational/personality predictions; mutually overlapping categories would break an exclusive classifier.

records.source_paraphrase: The author gives several meanings of upadeśa: reference, specification, instruction, advice and initiation; says sutra literature may refer to other śāstras.
records.caveat: A broad 'reference to other works' is NOT literal evidence that every Parashara or modern calculation is textually contained in a short Jaimini sutra.

book_sampling: Lessons 1,3,4,5 sampled from actual uploaded PDF33–88. Earlier batches sampled lessons2,6–22. All 22 lessons now have some reading, none exhaustive.
critical_boundaries: modern Rath interpretation versus literal Jaimini aphorisms
phonetic Sanskrit name data versus birth-only inputs
ritual instructional prescriptions versus observed natal outcomes
